hypothesis: Upgrading Decoupled Contrastive Learning (DCL) to DCL with Hard Negative Weighting (DCLW) will improve representation quality by downweighting false negative pairs while preserving strong repulsion for distinct negative pairs.
rationale: Iter 2 showed that DCL improves over InfoNCE (0.5396 vs 0.5310) by eliminating positive-pair terms from the loss denominator. Iter 4 further improved performance to 0.5419 with a 2-layer projection head. However, standard DCL treats all negative pairs equally in the exponential sum. In CIFAR-100, images from the same underlying class often act as negative pairs (false negatives) with high similarity z_i^T z_j ~ 1. DCLW (Yeh et al., CVPR 2022) scales negative pair contributions by their squared distance w_ij = 2 - 2 z_i^T z_j, suppressing false-negative repulsions and enhancing feature clustering within 50 epochs.
expected_effect: Validation linear-probe top-1 accuracy will increase beyond 0.5419.
change_summary: Updated `BarlowTwinsLoss` forward pass to compute DCLW loss using distance-based negative weighting w_ij = 2.0 - 2.0 * (z_i^T z_j), implemented stably via log-space addition `sim_neg + log(w_ij)` inside `logsumexp`.
